chunks: Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Yahya narrated from Abu Abdillah, from al-Sindi ibn Muhammad, from Abu al-Bakhtari Wahb ibn Wahb, from Ja'far ibn Muhammad, from his father (peace be upon him), who said:

Imam Ali (peace be upon him) ruled regarding a man who died and left heirs: if one of the heirs acknowledges a debt on behalf of his father, that debt binds him only in his share, proportional to what he inherited, and it does not become the entire burden on his wealth. If two of the heirs acknowledge it and they are just (reliable), the acknowledgment is accepted as binding on all the heirs. If they are not just, they are bound only in their shares, proportional to what they inherited. Similarly, if some of the heirs acknowledge the existence of a brother or sister, it binds them only in their share.

Imam Ali (peace be upon him) also said: 'Whoever acknowledges a brother for himself, he is a partner in the wealth but his lineage is not established. If two acknowledge, the same applies, unless they are just, in which case his lineage is established and he is included in the inheritance with them.'
ai.seo_question: How is a deceased father's debt distributed among heirs if only one heir acknowledges it?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* details Imam Ali’s jurisprudence on debt and lineage, establishing the principle of proportional liability for single heirs versus joint liability for two just witnesses. It highlights the Shia legal distinction between *iqrar* (acknowledgment) and *shahada* (testimony), where the status of the heirs as *adl* (just) determines whether lineage is confirmed and inheritance rights are fully activated.
